metal noun

also metals, made of metal, metallic

classical

Verg. A. 8.445: aurī (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 33.96 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 345
M-O s.v. metal (Egger)

metallum, metallī n.

noun, second declension

a metal; a mine

Its first sense is a mine or quarry, and the convict’s work in one (damnātus in metallum, Plin. Ep. 2.11.8); the metal dug from it is a sense of Vergil and Pliny (Lewis & Short). Latin often names the metal instead: aes for copper and bronze, ferrum for iron and steel (see steel).

Other words

  • metallicus, metallica, metallicum — of metal, metallic

    also used · post-classical · Plin. NH 34.173 (Lewis & Short)

    Pliny’s adjective; as a noun, a miner. Something made of metal is usually named by the metal: ferreus, aēneus, aureus.

Examples

  • fērācem frūgum, oleī, vīnī, equōrum metallōrumque omnium generum

    rich in grain, oil, wine, horses and metals of every kind (of Spain)Plin. NH 37.203

  • Illud aēneum cum pistillō ejusdem metallī.

    That bronze one, with the pestle of the same metal.Vīv. Exerc. 15 (not classical)

See also steel, gold, sheet metal, iron rod.
